fact: Seer is a prediction market platform that uses Reality.eth and the Conditional Tokens Framework to create and manage various market types.
quote: Seer is a prediction market platform that leverages Reality.eth and Conditional Tokens Framework to create and manage various types of markets.

fact: Seer allows users to create and participate in prediction markets for different events and outcomes.
quote: It allows users to create and participate in prediction markets for different events and outcomes.

fact: Categorical markets let users select one outcome from multiple options.
quote: Categorical Markets: Select one out of multiple outcomes.

fact: Multi-categorical markets are similar to categorical markets but allow selecting multiple outcomes.
quote: Multi-Categorical Markets: Similar to categorical market but allowing selection of multiple outcomes.

fact: Scalar markets use a numeric outcome within a specified range.
quote: Scalar Markets: Numeric outcome within a specified range.

fact: Multi-scalar markets involve multiple numeric outcomes.
Futarchy markets are used to make decisions based on a token’s predicted price.
quote: Futarchy Markets: To make decisions based on a token’s predicted price.

fact: The app navigation includes create market, verify market, mint/merge/redeem, buy/sell, report answer, raise dispute, resolve market, and provide liquidity actions.
quote: Create a market Verify market Mint, merge, redeem outcome tokens Buy, sell outcome tokens Report answer Raise a dispute Resolve market Provide Liquidity

fact: Reality.eth serves as Seer’s oracle system for resolving market outcomes.
quote: Seer uses Reality.eth as its oracle system for resolving market outcomes.

fact: Reality.eth questions are submitted with parameters such as opening time, timeout, and minimum bond.
quote: Questions are submitted to Reality.eth with specific parameters such as opening time, timeout, and minimum bond.

fact: Seer supports question templates including single-select, multi-select, and numeric scalar questions.
quote: The system supports multiple question templates, including single-select, multi-select, and numeric (scalar) questions.

fact: Seer uses the Conditional Tokens framework to create and manage outcome tokens.
quote: Seer utilizes the Conditional Tokens framework for creating and managing outcome tokens.

fact: Outcome tokens are represented as ERC1155 tokens within the Conditional Tokens system.
quote: Outcome tokens are represented as ERC1155 tokens within the Conditional Tokens system.

fact: Seer wraps ERC1155 outcome tokens into ERC20 tokens to improve usability, trading, and DeFi integration.
quote: To improve usability, Seer wraps the ERC1155 outcome tokens into ERC20 tokens. This allows for easier trading and integration with existing DeFi protocols.

fact: Kleros is used to resolve disputes that arise when answering Reality.eth questions.
quote: Seer uses Kleros to resolve disputes that may arise when answering Reality.eth questions.

fact: The Seer Solution section of the whitepaper is organized into subsections covering Seer DAO, retroactive public good funding, prediction market actors, token incentives, information seekers, exchange integration, and liquidity topics.
quote: Seer Solution Seer DAO Retroactive Public Good Funding Prediction Market Actors The Chicken and the egg problem Token Incentives Information Seekers Exchange Integration Liquidity Management

fact: Seer's governance model is a DAO described as decentralized governance in action, aimed at better and trustless results.
quote: Seer DAO Decentralised Governance in action, for better and trustless results.

fact: The whitepaper includes retroactive public good funding as a component of the Seer Solution.
Prediction market actors are treated as a distinct topic within the solution design.
The design addresses a 'chicken and egg problem' specific to prediction markets.
quote: The Chicken and the egg problem

fact: Token incentives are part of the proposed solution mechanics.
Information seekers are identified as a category of participant in the system.
Exchange integration is covered as part of the Seer Solution.
Liquidity management and safe liquidity provision are both separate topics addressed in the solution.
The practical implementation of Seer is described as a combination of an AMM and auctions.
Capital efficiency is presented as a rationale for the AMM + auctions implementation approach.
Lack of liquidity is framed as a core problem the solution is designed to address.
The whitepaper frames Seer's solution partly as a response to why previous prediction markets failed.
quote: Introduction to Seer Why previous prediction markets failed

fact: The documentation is split into Whitepaper and Developers sections and is hosted on the Mintlify developer documentation platform.
Seer is a prediction market platform built on Reality.eth and the Conditional Tokens Framework.
quote: Seer is a prediction market platform built on Reality.eth and the Conditional Tokens Framework.

fact: The Seer app includes a flow for creating a market.
Markets can be verified in the app.
Outcome tokens can be minted, merged, and redeemed.
Outcome tokens can be bought and sold.
Users can report an answer for a market.
Users can raise a dispute on a market.
Markets are resolved through a dedicated resolve step.
The app supports providing liquidity to markets.
Seer supports conditional markets, documented separately for app users.
Seer supports futarchy markets, documented separately for app users.

quote: Port an Omen trading agent to Seer: what changes, the market types, and the porting effort.

fact: Seer has collateral profiles supporting multi-primary collateral.
Deposit documentation includes DAI on Ethereum.
Seer contracts include a cross-chain Realitio foreign arbitration proxy with appeals.
